body.statement: Can the rank-adaptive spectral handle construct an estimator of \(\tau_{\omega}\) and a confidence interval with uniform asymptotic coverage over laws for which the smallest positive eigenvalue of \(H(X)\) approaches zero and the conditional rank changes on sets of positive probability, while reducing to \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{eff}}\) on every fixed-rank separated law?
body.justification: Rank changes are the natural nonregular boundary of the proposed efficiency theory and cannot be hidden inside a fixed-rank assumption.
body.gap: Newey (2001) gives generalized-inverse optimality under a stable conditional system, while the staggered DiD and DDD literatures do not provide rank-adaptive inference for learned conditional weights.
body.consumer: A rank-adaptive procedure would prevent unstable standard errors when empirical clean-comparison scores are nearly redundant.

obligation.what_is_open: A nontrivial uniformly valid, rank-adaptive confidence interval has not been characterized because the question does not specify a uniform law class, a length or power requirement, or local eigenvalue and nuisance-rate envelopes.
obligation.obstruction: At rank-changing laws the Moore--Penrose loading is discontinuous, while coverage alone admits the vacuous interval \(\mathbb R\).  Without a non-vacuity criterion and a local sequence class, the intended adaptation problem is not a well-posed mathematical yes-or-no statement.
obligation.attempted: The fixed-rank perturbation proof was extended to eigenvalues approaching zero.  Its bound necessarily contains the reciprocal selected eigenvalue, so neither the learned-loading remainder nor a stable Gaussian critical value is uniform.  A negative adaptation theorem would require a specified local experiment and an interval-length criterion; a positive theorem would require explicit eigenvalue-decay and learner-rate restrictions.
obligation.partial_result: On every fixed-rank law with positive spectrum separated by \(\kappa>0\), the existing threshold rule with \(r_{\Gamma,n}/\tau_n\to0\) recovers rank and gives the pointwise expansion proved for \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{eff}}\).  No uniform claim is made as \(\kappa\downarrow0\).
